bull_bear.body:
- Capability to deliver complex, high-voltage transformer/substation projects with precision, speed and reliability
- Strong, established base with public electricity utilities complemented by a diversifying customer base across national geographies
- Technology capability demonstrated by successful in-house design, manufacture, testing and commissioning of 400kV class transformers
- In-house manufacture and expanding product basket of Magnet Technology Machines / Synchronous AC Servo motors
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical conflict and oil-price shock (West Asia) — The surge in global crude oil prices since the West Asia conflict, exacerbated by supply disruptions, has tilted risks to inflation on the upside and growth on the downside, with financial-channel effects (safe-haven flows, higher borrowing costs) that could hinder private investment and overall economic growth.
- Raw material supply constraints and cost inflation for transformers — Global demand for power transformers continues to be strong, driving demand for requisite raw materials exponentially; certain critical inputs may face supply constraints or become costlier, pressuring input costs.
- Industry-wide transformer capacity oversupply — Since most domestic manufacturers are expanding transformer capacity, such expanded capacity, in the absence of sustained demand, may exacerbate price competition in the industry.
- Currency depreciation and import cost pressure — Further widening of the current account deficit and capital outflows may lead to currency depreciation, adding to inflationary pressures through higher import prices.
- Global trade-policy and tariff uncertainty — Geopolitical tensions, volatility in global financial markets, and uncertainty surrounding global trade policies could pose headwinds to growth and inflation, compounded by weather-related disruptions.
- Competitive intensity compressing segment margins — The electrical motors business faces severe headwinds of intense competition that kept prices depressed despite volume growth, adversely affecting segmental margins; the Magnet Technology Machines business similarly faces severe price competition from imported brands, hurting profitability.
- Rising leverage and interest-cost sensitivity — The Debt Equity Ratio increased sharply (to 0.15 from 0.04, up 275%) due to higher working capital borrowings and lower operating profits, while the Interest Coverage Ratio declined (to 10.28 from 14.36) on higher borrowing cost, increasing sensitivity to credit conditions.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company designs, manufactures, commissions and markets power transformers and undertakes EPC projects for electrical substations (delivery, rectification, commissioning and servicing of transformers, plus maintenance products) under its Power Systems segment. Its Industrial Systems segment develops, manufactures and markets standard and customised electric motors, magnet technology machines (including synchronous AC servo motors), and engineering/supply of drives and automation solutions. It operates exclusively in the Business-to-Business segment, serving industrial enterprises, original equipment manufacturers and government organisations.

- **Industrial Systems:** Standard and customised electric motors, Smoke Extraction Motors (BS EN 12101-3:2015), Magnet Technology Machines, Synchronous AC Servo motors, Drives and automation solutions, IE4 range induction motors, Traction motors

outlook.body:
- Strengthen market share across the full range of transformer voltage classes following successful entry into 400kV class manufacturing, and grow the newly-won ester oil transformer line
- Projects business to pursue larger-sized projects as the next phase of growth and to specifically target booking of 400kV projects, a market not yet addressed
- Grow e-mobility orders and use PLI scheme benefits plus component localization to pass on cost benefits to customers; expand into new verticals of metals, printing and packaging beyond the predominant plastics segment in Drives & Automation
- Localize manufacture of drives components to mitigate currency/margin pressure
- Improve market reach in the domestic gearless machines market for Magnet Technology Machines, with supply chain optimization and inventory management initiatives
- Continue diversifying and widening the transformer customer base across national geographies to complement the strong existing base in public electricity utilities
- Industrial Systems (motors) focus on widening market reach, refining the supply chain, and developing energy-efficient, economical products
- Continuously invest in enlarging technologically advanced, superior and sustainable product offerings and augmenting facilities to capitalise on emerging opportunities
- Projects business strategy of selecting quality projects and pursuing execution excellence, leveraging capability to deliver complex, high-voltage projects with precision, speed and reliability
- The Company maintains a formal Dividend Distribution Policy (as required under SEBI Listing Regulation 43A for top-1000 listed entities by market capitalisation), under which the Board weighs various factors in recommending the annual dividend. Capacity expansion (Airoli transformer capacity) is being funded entirely out of internal accruals rather than fresh debt. The Company has not accepted or renewed any fixed deposits from the public. Credit rating for bank facilities has been maintained at ICRA AA- (Stable, Long Term) and ICRA A1+ (Short Term).
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company is expanding transformer manufacturing capacity at its Airoli works (Navi Mumbai). The original plan, intimated in the prior Annual Report, was to raise capacity from 18,000 MVA to 28,000 MVA at an outlay of about ₹170 crore; considering conducive market conditions, management revised the plan upward to 35,000 MVA at a total outlay of ₹235 crore, to be funded entirely out of internal accruals. During the year the Company successfully entered manufacturing of 400kV class transformers, secured orders for that class, began execution and commissioned a few units. Separately, on the ESG/capex-mix side, the Company reported that 12.73% of its capital expenditure in FY2025-26 (down from 22.05% in FY2024-25) went toward technologies improving environmental and social impact, citing Design Optimisation in Motors as having simplified the manufacturing process and reduced environmental impact.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's total installed power generation capacity has surged to 525 GW (March 2026); National Electricity Plan (2023-2032) targets 458 GW peak demand by 2032, expanding transmission network from 4.98 lakh ckm to 6.48 lakh ckm and transformation capacity from 1,398 GVA to 2,345 GVA — a multi-year structural driver for the transformer industry
- Large renewable-energy capacity addition, industrial expansion, public infrastructure projects (metro lines, railway electrification, EV charging stations, data centers) and overall grid strengthening continue to drive growth for the transformer industry
- Indian electric motors market projected to maintain a decent growth rate; stricter government regulations and ESG-related compliance are driving replacement of older, inefficient motors with high-efficiency alternatives
- Increasing manufacturing automation and government initiatives (Make in India, PLI) are increasing demand for AC motors, with high-demand areas including HVAC, home appliances, automotive, mining, water and power generation
- Global and local demand for power transformers continues to be strong, with the demand-supply situation remaining favourable to industry players
- Government programs — inter-regional transmission grid upgradation, National Green Hydrogen Mission, battery energy storage (BESS) and pumped storage plants (PSPs), and Revamped Distribution Sector Schemes — are driving power network upgradation and demand for power equipment
- Motors market witnessed growth in H2FY26 better than earlier quarters, along with price increases across players to pass on commodity inflation
- Domestic economic activity remained resilient, driven by private consumption (rural and urban), GST rate rationalisation and monetary easing, with manufacturing strengthening on the supply side
- Transformer business unexecuted order book grew by 40% year-on-year, alongside record production and dispatch statistics
- Projects business registered 37% year-on-year growth with on-time, within-budget execution and continued repeat orders from marquee industry names
- Received an important traction motor order from Indian Railways, with hopes to build on this in future
- E-mobility orders under execution with the segment growing at a rapid rate

deepdive.thesis: Bharat Bijlee is a B2B electrical engineering manufacturer serving India's power and industrial markets through two segments — Power Systems (power transformers and substation EPC) and Industrial Systems (electric motors, magnet technology machines, drives and automation).

open.item: Capacity expansion of the transformer manufacturing facility at Airoli works, revised from an original target of 28,000 MVA (₹170 crore outlay) to 35,000 MVA at a total outlay of ₹235 crore, funded entirely from internal accruals.

Having entered manufacturing of 400kV class transformers this year (orders secured and units commissioned), the Company's focus is to further strengthen market share and serve the entire range of transformer voltage classes, including a first order received for ester oil transformers.
Transformer business continues its strategy of diversifying and widening its customer base across national geographies to complement its strong existing base in public electricity utilities.
Since most domestic manufacturers are expanding transformer capacity, such expanded capacity, absent sustained demand, may exacerbate price competition in the industry.

Electrical motors business continues to face severe headwinds of intense competition depressing prices despite volume growth; Magnet Technology Machines business faces severe price competition from imported brands, adversely affecting profitability.
Focus will be to further strengthen market share and serve the entire range of transformers, building on the newly commissioned 400kV class and the first order received for ester oil transformers.
Next phase of growth for the Projects business will come from larger sized projects being targeted, with a specific focus on booking 400kV projects, a large market not so far addressed.

Company will use the benefits of the PLI scheme and localization to pass on cost benefits to customers in e-mobility, and will focus on metals, printing and packaging as new verticals in the Drives and Automation business.
Company has significantly improved its market reach in the domestic gearless machines market and expects an increase in volume in the near future for the Magnet Technology Machines business.
The Euro appreciated about 17% year-on-year, which has severely impacted margins in the Drives and Automation business.
Magnet Technology Machines business has been severely impacted by the ongoing trade war and geo-economic issues; specific grades of magnets are still difficult to obtain.
